findings.issue: `Pion.conj` (546) and `Pion.valence` (558) are pattern-matching defs with no equation lemmas, while `PionFlavor.swap` right above gets `swap_up`/`swap_down` (523, 527). Nothing public says `Pion.conj .plus = .minus` or `Species.quark .up ∈ Pion.valence .plus`, so the π⁻/π⁰ content advertised in the module docstring (line 45) is unreachable downstream, as is `favoured_conj_of_chargeConjRelation` applied at `.plus` (its result mentions `pionContent.conj .plus`, which cannot be reduced).

summary: The new file is a non-exposed `public section` (Symmetries.lean:87), so definition bodies are invisible downstream, yet the two named relations, `IsValenceFlavor`, `partonConj`, `Pion.conj` and `Pion.valence` ship without the unfolding/equation lemmas the repo gives every other def in that situation (`momentumSumRule_iff`, `chargeConj_eq_comap`, `Species.conj_quark`, and this PR's own `favoured_def`/`swap_up`). As published, a consumer can neither establish nor apply `ChargeConjRelation`/`FlavorRelation`, and nothing public states the antiparticle or valence content of any pion.
